key_insight: Global relaxed entropy-energy states can be constructed even when the temperature-dependent yield set collapses, but macroscopic Prandtl–Reuss normality is not guaranteed.
engineering_relevance: The analysis clarifies how idealized dynamic thermoplastic models behave when thermal weakening eliminates deviatoric yield resistance.
method: One-parameter Temam–Norton–Hoff–Galerkin approximation with an undiscretized heat equation.
Entropy-weighted estimates establish temperature compactness and stress admissibility.
Measure-based compact-fibre lifts preserve exact normality and maximum plastic work.
evidence_signal: Analytical results include an O(√(log n/n)) overstress convergence rate in each fixed finite Lebesgue space and an explicit smooth counterexample to macroscopic normality.
watch_item: The available compactness does not identify a canonical macroscopic stress–plastic-flow pairing; fully collapsed regimes can also lose finite-measure plastic flow or full displacement boundary traces.
paper_title: Dynamic Prandtl-Reuss Thermoplasticity with Degenerating Yield Constraints
